title: When to Use Encode-Prefill-Decode Disaggregation to Accelerate Multimodal Model Serving | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's Dynamo inference framework separates vision encoding from LLM prefill/decode (EPD disaggregation), cutting TTFT up to 58-93% and boosting same-SLO goodput up to 2.64x for image-heavy, small/quantized, mixed-traffic multimodal serving workloads — but the technique loses or reverses its edge as output length grows or model size increases past ~27B, revealing goodput economics as a moving target that depends heavily on hardware tiering and model precision choices.

themes.theme: EPD disaggregation architecture and hardware tiering

insights.claim: NVIDIA Dynamo's encode-prefill-decode (EPD) disaggregation splits multimodal inference into three independently scalable stages — vision encoding, LLM prefill, and decode — connected via the NVIDIA Inference Transfer Library (NIXL), instead of running all stages on one GPU under one scheduler as in aggregated serving.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Establishes a general disaggregation pattern (already proven for prefill/decode) now extending to the encoder stage — infra vendors and inference-serving startups should expect this three-way split to become a standard topology for multimodal serving stacks.
insights.quote: Dynamo implements EPD serving by separating the encoder and PD worker roles without fixing their hardware placement.

insights.claim: Dynamo supports three encoder placement topologies — aggregated (all stages on one GPU), colocated encoder (encoder and PD workers share the same GPU class with separate queues), and disaggregated encoder (encoder runs on a separate, cheaper GPU tier) — and the disaggregated-on-homogeneous-hardware combination always underperforms colocated, so it is excluded from the analysis.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Signals a concrete new demand channel for lower-tier/older GPUs (e.g., RTX 6000D-class) as dedicated encoder capacity in heterogeneous clusters, rather than idling them or retiring them — relevant to secondary-market GPU demand and NVIDIA's tiered product strategy.
insights.quote: In our test environment, two NVIDIA RTX 6000D GPUs ran the encoder workers, while four NVIDIA GB200 GPUs ran the PD workers.

insights.claim: Hardware availability determines where the encoder can physically run, while workload characteristics (media load, output length, model size/precision, traffic mix) determine whether disaggregating it actually pays off — so the placement decision is a two-variable optimization, not a fixed best practice.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Investors modeling inference infrastructure ROI should treat EPD/disaggregation gains as workload-conditional, not a blanket efficiency win — due diligence on any vendor claiming disaggregation speedups should ask which of these four factors dominates their production traffic.
insights.quote: Hardware availability determines where the encoder can run and workload characteristics determine whether separating it pays off.

insights.claim: EPD disaggregation delivers up to 5x faster time-to-first-token (TTFT) and up to 7x faster end-to-end response time versus aggregated serving for image-heavy prompts, short-to-medium outputs, and quantized mixture-of-experts models specifically — not as a universal multiplier across all workloads.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: The 5x/7x headline figures are best-case, workload-specific numbers investors should not extrapolate to all multimodal inference deployments — actual gains depend on the traffic mix a given customer runs.
insights.quote: This post shows when and how to use EPD disaggregation with NVIDIA Dynamo to achieve up to 5x faster time to first token (TTFT) and 7x faster end-to-end response time.

insights.claim: In a 10-images-per-request, OSL-1024 test on four GB200 GPUs, TTFT dropped 58% with colocated encoder and 50% with disaggregated (heterogeneous) encoder versus aggregated serving, while end-to-end gains were modest because decode time was unaffected by encoder disaggregation; the heterogeneous tier served 70% more traffic at the same ITL-under-100ms SLO.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: The 70% goodput gain came from adding cheap encoder capacity without touching the GB200 budget — a concrete capacity-planning lever: buy lower-tier GPUs for encoding rather than more GB200s to raise throughput under a fixed latency SLO.
insights.quote: TTFT drops 58% with colocated encoder and 50% with heterogeneous. ... the heterogeneous tier serves 70% more traffic at the same latency SLO, because encoder capacity was added without touching the GB200 budget.

insights.claim: Across a grid of 5-50 images and varying output sequence lengths, both EPD topologies deliver 25-93% TTFT improvement over aggregated serving on Qwen3.5 122B A10B NVFP4, with the heaviest tested load (50 images x 128 tokens) reaching 92-93% TTFT reduction regardless of output length, since TTFT is unaffected by output length.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Gives investors a quantified ceiling (up to 93% TTFT cut) for image-heavy multimodal serving economics, useful for benchmarking rival inference stacks (vLLM, SGLang) once they ship equivalent EPD features.
insights.quote: Both topologies deliver 25-93% TTFT improvement across the full grid. The heaviest cell (50 x 128 images, any OSL) reaches 92-93%.

themes.theme: Where EPD gains erode or reverse

insights.claim: As output sequence length (OSL) grows from 128 to 2,048 tokens at fixed 5-image load, decode time increasingly dominates total latency, causing heterogeneous EPD's end-to-end gain over aggregated serving to narrow from 20.3% to 5.2%, while colocated encoder's gain flips from an 11.8% improvement to a 2.5% regression because its encoder workers compete for the same GPUs as the PD workers.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Colocated EPD can actively hurt performance for long-output workloads (e.g., long-form multimodal reasoning/chat) — a concrete gotcha for any vendor deploying EPD without first profiling output-length distribution.
insights.quote: Co-located encoder shifts from an 11.8% gain to a 2.5% regression because its additional encoder workers share the same GPUs as the PD workers.
insights.locator: How do image load and OSL impact performance gains?

insights.claim: As LLM model size grows from 4B to 27B parameters with vision-encoder size held roughly fixed, the ViT parameter share falls from 7.2% to 1.7%, and colocated EPD's goodput multiple over aggregated serving falls correspondingly from 2.62x to 1.50x to 0.65x — meaning EPD becomes a net negative (below break-even) at the 27B scale tested.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Large dense multimodal models are the wrong target for EPD disaggregation investment — vendors and infra buyers should reserve this optimization for small/MoE/quantized model deployments, not frontier-scale dense LLMs.
insights.quote: EPD gain decreases with model size and falls below break-even at 27B.

insights.claim: Quantizing only the active LLM weights from BF16 to NVFP4 while keeping the vision encoder in BF16 increased colocated EPD's goodput advantage over aggregated serving from 1.78x to 2.64x, because NVFP4 accelerates LLM prefill/decode while ViT compute stays fixed, shifting a larger relative share of request time to encoder work that EPD can then schedule independently.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Quantization strategy and disaggregation architecture are complementary, not independent levers — NVIDIA's NVFP4 precision format directly compounds EPD's infrastructure ROI, reinforcing NVIDIA's push toward FP4 adoption across its Blackwell-class hardware stack.
insights.quote: Quantizing the active LM weights from BF16 to NVFP4 increased the ratio from 1.78x to 2.64x. The vision encoder remained in BF16 in both configurations.

insights.claim: Under sustained 50:50 mixed text/image traffic at OSL 128, encoder disaggregation reduced mean TTFT for text-only requests from 92.3ms to 53.3ms (a 42.2% reduction) and for image requests from 289.9ms to 200.6ms (a 30.8% reduction), because aggregated serving forces text requests to wait behind vision-encoding work in the same scheduling batch (head-of-line blocking) while EPD lets text requests skip straight to prefill.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: Any production LLM API serving a blended text+multimodal traffic mix (e.g., a consumer chatbot with optional image upload) has a quantified latency-SLA case for EPD even independent of pure multimodal throughput gains — a distinct adoption driver from the image-heavy use case.
insights.quote: Encoder disaggregation reduced mean TTFT for text requests from 92.3 to 53.3 ms, a 42.2% reduction. Image-request TTFT fell from 289.9 to 200.6 ms, a 30.8% reduction.
insights.locator: How EPD helps mixed modality requests

themes.theme: Competitive landscape and further optimization levers

insights.claim: Competing inference-serving frameworks vLLM and SGLang both have roadmaps for developing their own EPD disaggregation stacks, indicating encode-stage disaggregation is becoming a contested feature area across the open-source inference serving ecosystem rather than a Dynamo-exclusive capability.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's first-mover EPD implementation in Dynamo faces imminent feature parity from vLLM and SGLang, so its competitive moat here is likely time-limited — watch for those projects shipping equivalent capabilities within 1-2 quarters.
insights.quote: Note that vLLM and SGLang have roadmaps for further development of their EPD stacks.
insights.locator: How to select the best encoder topology

insights.claim: Even with EPD active, 43% of TTFT is spent before vision-transformer processing even starts (media download/preprocessing), a stage EPD does not address; enabling parallel media decoding (moving download/decode into the Dynamo front end) cut mean encoder request latency by 26% (281.3ms to 207.0ms) and P99 latency by 23% (752.1ms to 581.7ms) in a 30-image, two-encoder-worker benchmark on one GB200.
insights.speaker: Jesse Gu
insights.so_what: EPD disaggregation alone leaves a large chunk of latency (pre-ViT media handling) on the table; investors should view Dynamo's full lever stack (EPD + parallel media decoding + embedding cache + multimodal KV routing) as the real product, not any single feature in isolation.
insights.quote: As shown in Figure 1, 43% of TTFT was spent before ViT even started. EPD does not help optimize those stages of the pipeline.
